questions: Verify print mode, sessions, automatic context compaction and schema/report extraction.
Check accounting, interruption and permission boundaries against pinned upstream code.
decision: Add version-aware Kimi command contracts before changing flags: the current and legacy documentation describe materially different non-interactive modes.
code_observations: The existing Kimi worker appends a configured permission flag and --prompt. The current official command reference says --prompt cannot be combined with --yolo, --auto or --plan.

The legacy reference instead documents --print and its own non-interactive semantics. This is a documentation/source incompatibility risk, not a reproduced failure of an installed CLI in this environment.
implementation_steps: Introduce bounded version/help discovery and explicit supported protocol variants. Never combine flags from the old and new references.
For a current variant, construct the documented non-interactive invocation and handle its permission boundary explicitly; for a legacy variant, retain only the tested compatible syntax.
Normalize stream-json messages into terminal outcome, bounded report and usage. Intermediate text, context-compaction events and tool output are not a completion artifact.
Treat session reuse as opt-in with documented storage/retention; default cross-provider continuation remains an evidence capsule and the worktree.
Add a diagnostic that identifies unknown versions without silently switching to unrestricted operation. Preserve user configuration and never run an automatic upgrade.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Current fixtures reject --prompt combined with obsolete or mutually exclusive permission flags.
Legacy fixtures keep their documented print-mode syntax instead of receiving current-only flags.
A missing terminal report, malformed JSONL or interrupted stream cannot pass acceptance.
Budget, transient and permanent errors are normalized only when the version contract establishes their meaning.
Session identifiers and logs never introduce secrets into a shared handoff.

alternatives.title: Reuse one permission/prompt combination
alternatives.tradeoff: May work on a pinned release but is not portable across documented protocol changes.

alternatives.title: Version-qualified minimal adapter variants
alternatives.tradeoff: Small targeted maintenance cost and an explicit unsupported-version result.

alternatives.title: Blindly add --print because an older page mentions it
alternatives.tradeoff: Can fix one version while breaking another; unsupported changes are not evidence-based.

cost_model: Version/help probes are deterministic and cached. Avoid paid calls to discover a syntax error; use fixtures before an explicitly authorized live smoke test.
unverified: No installed Kimi executable was run, so actual compatibility must be confirmed with its version/help and one bounded authorized test.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated model calls; tests listed here are implementation obligations, not claimed passes.
